subject: [hw] T01 -> lead: V19 VSHN corrupts lanes when Vd overlaps Vm (clean repro, likely root of the vector failures)
body:
Found it, and it is a real V19 overlap bug, not VMOVN semantics. Repro (thumb, current tree):

  movw r4,#0x5678; movt r4,#0x1234; vdup.32 q0,r4   @ q0 = 12345678 x4
  vshrn.i32 d1,q0,#8        @ dest d1 overlaps source q0 (d0,d1)
  vmov r0,r1,d1
  expected 3456345634563456; got 3456345656343456 (lane 2 corrupted)

With a non-overlapping destination (`vshrn.i32 d4,q0,#8`, q0 = 11111111/22222222/33333333/44444444 per lane) the result is correct, so the decode/shift is fine; the implementation writes destination lanes while still reading source lanes. ARM allows Vd == Vm and reads all source operands before writing. Fix: copy the 128-bit source to a local uint64_t src[2] (or uint8_t[16]) before the loop and call vec_get on that copy, or buffer all results and write after. The same pattern likely affects the other narrow/shift/widen loops in n2a32_neon_shift.c that write Vd while reading Vm (VMOVN, VSHLL/VMOVL, VADDL/VADDW/VSUBL, VMLAL/VMLSL, etc.) - I can supply overlap repros for each if useful.

This explains k_i16_loop/k_i16_mul/k_i8_loop/k_neon_vmla16/k_neon_vsubl all failing at arm-O2 (their compiler output reuses low registers for in-place shifts/narrows). k18_select is now fixed by V20s VEXT. V19 is finished; can you patch it (or wake V19)? My harness will re-run immediately.
